answer: A convincing sybil defense ties rewards to vested payouts across many epochs, like a comet brightening only after long orbits. Each agent's earnings lock in a lotus-like vault that drips over 100 epochs; a flash-farm identity leaves with under 1% of its yield, the rest forfeited on exit. To profit, an attacker must keep every fake mesa outpost bonded, alive, and honest for months, paying capital lockup and slash risk per identity - so impersonation costs more than it earns, and one long-lived honest identity beats a thousand disposable ones.
